classification.difficultyReason: Introduce a perpendicular projection, eliminate its height from two Pythagorean equations, then recover the height and use a third triangle to find the exact distance.

content.prompt: A rectangle $ABCD$ has $AB=15\text{ cm}$, $AD=10\text{ cm}$. A point $P$ is located inside the rectangle such that $AP=14\text{ cm}$ and $PB=11\text{ cm}$. Find $PD$ in exact form.

answer.short:
$2\sqrt{74-20\sqrt6}\text{ cm}$.

Use a perpendicular from $P$ to $AB$ and compare the two resulting Pythagorean equations.
answer.worked:
Let $H$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $P$ to $AB$, with $AH=t\text{ cm}$ and $PH=s\text{ cm}$. Then $HB=(15-t)\text{ cm}$.

Pythagoras’ theorem gives $t^2+s^2=196$ and $(15-t)^2+s^2=121$. Subtracting,

$$\begin{align*}t^2-(15-t)^2&=196-121\\30t-225&=75\\30t&=300\\t&=10\end{align*}$$

Hence

$$\begin{align*}s^2&=196-10^2\\s^2&=96\\s&=4\sqrt6\end{align*}$$

The perpendicular distances separating $P$ and $D$ are $10\text{ cm}$ parallel to $AB$ and $(10-4\sqrt6)\text{ cm}$ parallel to $AD$. Therefore,

$$\begin{align*}PD^2&=10^2+(10-4\sqrt6)^2\\PD^2&=100+100-80\sqrt6+96\\PD^2&=296-80\sqrt6\\PD&=2\sqrt{74-20\sqrt6}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
